study_material.title: Synonyms - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: A synonym is a word with the same or nearly the same meaning as another. Placement tests use synonyms to measure vocabulary depth. Since rote memorisation is slow, combine high-frequency word lists with root-word logic and context reasoning.
learning_objectives: Use Latin and Greek roots to decode unfamiliar words
Apply prefix logic to narrow meaning
Eliminate options using connotation and part of speech

concepts.heading: 1. Root Words
concepts.body: Roots unlock hundreds of words. BENE (good): benevolent, benefactor, beneficial. MAL (bad): malevolent, malice, malfunction. CRED (believe): credible, incredulous, credentials. VOC/VOKE (call): vocation, evoke, revoke. LOQU/LOC (speak): loquacious, eloquent, colloquial. PHIL (love): philanthropy, bibliophile. FID (faith): fidelity, confide, perfidy.

concepts.heading: 2. Prefixes
concepts.body: Negative prefixes flip meaning: un-, in-, im-, ir-, il-, dis-, non-, a-. Direction/degree: sub- (under), super-/supra- (above), inter- (between), intra- (within), ante- (before), post- (after), circum- (around), trans- (across). Spotting 'ab-' in 'abhor' or 'anti-' in 'antipathy' points to a negative sense.

concepts.heading: 3. Connotation
concepts.body: Near-synonyms differ in tone. 'Thrifty' is positive; 'stingy' is negative; both relate to spending little. 'Confident' vs 'arrogant'. When two options share a denotation, pick the one whose tone matches the question word.

concepts.heading: 4. Part of Speech Matching
concepts.body: The answer must match the question word's part of speech. If the given word is an adjective, eliminate noun options immediately - this alone often halves the choices.

concepts.heading: 5. High-Frequency List
concepts.body: Abundant = plentiful. Candid = frank. Diligent = hardworking. Eloquent = articulate. Frugal = thrifty. Gregarious = sociable. Hostile = unfriendly. Imminent = impending. Lucid = clear. Meticulous = careful. Novice = beginner. Obsolete = outdated. Prudent = wise. Reluctant = unwilling. Scrutinise = examine. Tenacious = persistent. Vivid = bright. Zealous = enthusiastic.

formulas: BENE = good, MAL = bad, CRED = believe, LOQU = speak
Negative prefixes: un-, in-, im-, ir-, il-, dis-, non-, a-
Match part of speech before meaning
Tone must match: positive word needs a positive synonym
shortcut_methods: Break the word into prefix + root + suffix
Place the word in a sentence you know, then test each option in that sentence
Eliminate by part of speech first, then by tone
common_mistakes: Choosing an antonym under time pressure - read the instruction carefully
Ignoring connotation and picking a technically close but tonally wrong word
study_material.summary: Learn roots and prefixes to decode unknown words, then filter options by part of speech and tone.

solved_examples.question: Choose the synonym of ABUNDANT.
solved_examples.step_by_step: Abundant means existing in large quantity - plentiful. The others are antonyms.
solved_examples.shortcut: Three options are all near-synonyms of each other (scarce/empty/limited) - the odd one out is the answer.

solved_examples.question: Choose the synonym of CANDID.
solved_examples.step_by_step: Candid means openly honest and straightforward - frank.
solved_examples.shortcut: Think of a 'candid photo' - unposed, natural, honest.

solved_examples.question: Choose the synonym of BENEVOLENT.
solved_examples.step_by_step: The root BENE means 'good', so benevolent means well-wishing or kind.

solved_examples.question: Choose the synonym of METICULOUS.
solved_examples.step_by_step: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail - careful and precise.

solved_examples.question: Choose the synonym of LOQUACIOUS.
solved_examples.step_by_step: The root LOQU means 'to speak', so loquacious describes someone who talks a great deal.

practice_questions.question: Choose the synonym of DILIGENT.
practice_questions.explanation: Diligent means showing persistent, careful effort.

practice_questions.question: Choose the synonym of VIVID.
practice_questions.explanation: Vivid means intensely bright or clear.

practice_questions.question: Choose the synonym of NOVICE.
practice_questions.explanation: A novice is new to an activity.

practice_questions.question: Choose the synonym of HOSTILE.
practice_questions.explanation: Hostile means showing opposition or dislike.

practice_questions.question: Choose the synonym of FRUGAL.
practice_questions.explanation: Frugal means economical with money or resources.

practice_questions.question: Choose the synonym of GREGARIOUS.
practice_questions.explanation: Gregarious describes someone who enjoys company.

practice_questions.question: Choose the synonym of OBSOLETE.
practice_questions.explanation: Obsolete means no longer in use.

practice_questions.question: Choose the synonym of TENACIOUS.
practice_questions.explanation: Tenacious means holding firmly and not giving up.

practice_questions.question: Choose the synonym of EPHEMERAL.
practice_questions.explanation: Ephemeral means lasting a very short time.

practice_questions.question: Choose the synonym of PRAGMATIC.
practice_questions.explanation: Pragmatic means dealing with things sensibly and realistically.

topic_test.title: Synonyms - Topic Test
instructions: +1 for correct, -0.25 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.
Read carefully - these ask for SYNONYMS, not antonyms.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of RELUCTANT.
questions.explanation: Reluctant means hesitant to do something.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of ELOQUENT.
questions.explanation: Eloquent means fluent and persuasive in speech.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of SCRUTINISE.
questions.explanation: To scrutinise is to inspect closely.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of PRUDENT.
questions.explanation: Prudent means showing care and good judgement.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of ZEALOUS.
questions.explanation: Zealous means showing great energy for a cause.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of AMBIGUOUS.
questions.explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of ALLEVIATE.
questions.explanation: To alleviate is to make suffering less severe.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of INDIGENOUS.
questions.explanation: Indigenous means originating naturally in a place.
